idiom_name: case class + derived codecs (circe / Play JSON / upickle)
implementation_notes: A case class is Scala's native data carrier - constructor, accessors, equals/hashCode, copy and pattern matching for free - so the classic bean is replaced by one line, while serialization comes from a codec library that derives Encoder/Decoder (circe) or Reads/Writes/Format (Play JSON, upickle) from the case class. Derivation is compile-time and type-directed: the macro or given instances fail the build when a nested type has no codec, turning wire-contract mistakes into compile errors. Keep the codecs next to the case class or in the boundary module so the wire shape has exactly one owner.
code_sketch:
import play.api.libs.json._

case class OrderDto(id: Long, customer: String, lines: List[LineDto])
implicit val format: OFormat[OrderDto] = Json.format[OrderDto]

val wire = Json.toJson(OrderDto(1, "Ada", Nil)).toString
val back = Json.fromJson[OrderDto](Json.parse(wire))   // JsResult
pitfalls: Default parameter values and Option fields do not automatically mean "optional on the wire": each codec library decides how absent defaults and None are represented, so absence semantics must be pinned explicitly.

Derivation macros need the full static type and fail on recursive or abstract hierarchies without hand-written codecs; very large case classes can still trip arity or implicit-resolution limits in some derivation paths.
Case classes are shallowly immutable - a var or mutable collection member is still mutable - and structural equality makes accidental deep comparisons cheap to write but not free.
